447	## Phase 2b: Instrument for the PROMOTE-time broad coverage (not a dashboard widen)
448	
449	The "proper", beyond-the-PR coverage does NOT run on the dashboard. It runs once, automatically, at
450	**promote** (when a merged PR's spec becomes a component): Studio writes the component config with a
451	**broad** `testCommand` (parallel where the logging is buffered, serial where it is live) and runs
452	the oracle in the background. The dashboard then just displays
453	the spec-relevant traces and lets you re-run that same config. There is no "Run full test suite" widen
454	agent. So your job in the PR instrument step is to annotate so that promote's broad run finds everything
455	**without any re-instrumentation**. Two conditions must BOTH hold for a test in another crate to
456	contribute a trace:
457	
458	1. **Code annotation lives in shared LIBRARY code.** The `logAction` calls must sit in the
459	   application/library code other crates actually execute — NOT in this crate's test wrappers (the
460	   Philosophy rule). Then any crate calling that library — including the integration suite — emits
461	   automatically. Verify this; it is what makes broad coverage possible at all.
462	2. **Each candidate test carries a `startTest` boundary, registered up front.** Buffered logs (the
463	   transition fires on the test's own thread) are flushed TAGGED with their test name, so such tests
464	   are attribution-safe under full parallelism — threads AND process-parallel runners (nextest, jest
465	   workers). Only tests whose transitions fire off the test's own thread (an async/actor test on a
466	   `tokio` worker) fall back to live untagged logs into the daemon's serial slot — **those must run
467	   serially** (in Rust, `--test-threads=1`). Scope the serial constraint to the async suites instead
468	   of blanketing the whole command: a sync-only unit-test target may keep its parallelism. When
469	   unsure whether transitions run off-thread, keep that target serial. A test with no boundary
470	   contributes **zero** traces.
471	   - **JS/TS:** a `beforeEach`/global setup hook blankets a package; wire the same shared hook into each
472	     package whose tests should report.
473	   - **Rust:** no global per-test hook — each test binds the guard (`let _t =
474	     quint_oracle_client::start_test("…")`). Reuse a **shared helper** rather than editing tests
475	     ad-hoc — e.g. the integration suite's `quint_oracle_guard(name)` (in `tests/it/main.rs`); add one
476	     where a crate lacks it. Only crates whose tests adopt the helper contribute coverage.
477	
478	**Record the broad scope as `studio.broadTestCommand`.** The promote-time broad run must cover every
479	test target/package whose tests exercise this spec — **including any integration-test target** (an
480	async/end-to-end suite is usually the only place cross-component behavior is driven). Keep it
481	PARALLEL wherever the logging is buffered (tagged flushes attribute correctly across workers and
482	processes); force serial ONLY on the suites that live-log. Write it as a single **array-form**
483	command (like `testCommand`), scoped to exactly the targets/tests below and expressed in your
484	runner's own flags — e.g. Jest `["jest","cart/","sync/"]`, pytest
485	`["pytest","tests/cart","tests/sync"]`, Rust `["cargo","nextest","run","-p","cart","-p","integration"]`
486	(append the serial flag — `--runInBand` / `-p no:xdist` / `--test-threads=1` — only when that
487	target live-logs). It MUST go under `studio`
488	(quint's strict config parser rejects unknown top-level keys; `studio` is a pass-through metadata blob);
489	Studio runs it VERBATIM at promote, so it works for any runner. If you omit it, promote reuses the PR
490	`testCommand` as-is — so either set `broadTestCommand` or make the PR command broad enough. If you omit
491	a target, its tests won't run at promote and that coverage is lost.
492	
493	**Estimate the scope — which packages AND tests actually touch this spec.** Don't run the whole
494	project (or a whole integration target of hundreds of tests, most contributing nothing) — but don't
495	under-scope either: **the relevant set is exactly the tests that carry the oracle boundary guard**, and
496	they are usually SCATTERED across many modules, not one. The decisive signal is the guard, not the
497	module name.
498	1. Take the library function(s) you put `log_action` in (your Phase 2 edits).
499	2. `Grep the WHOLE integration target for the boundary` (`start_test` / the repo's boundary helper such
500	   as `quint_oracle_guard`) — every test that binds it is a contributor and MUST be in scope.
501	   (Uninstrumented tests produce no trace, so you don't need them — and that's the only reason you can
502	   narrow at all.)
503	3. Scope the broad command to keep the cheap in-process unit tests whole AND include EVERY guarded
504	   integration test — using your runner's own selectors (a Jest/pytest path or `-t` name filter, a
505	   nextest **filterset**, …). Don't scope to a single module — one that drops guarded modules silently
506	   drops the families only those tests cover; include ALL the guarded modules. For **Rust** the filter
507	   is a nextest filterset passed to `cargo nextest run … -E <expr>` — e.g.
508	   `not package(arc-malachitebft-test) | test(value_sync)` is WRONG if `full_nodes`, `reset`,
509	   `validity_change`, … also carry guards; use
510	   `not package(arc-malachitebft-test) | test(value_sync) | test(full_node) | test(n3f1) |
511	   test(reset_height) | test(persistent_peers_only) | test(vote_rebroadcast) | test(validity_change)`.
512	4. Record the scope. In Quint Studio's PR flow you do NOT hand-write the config — pass the full
513	   broad argv array (scoped to the targets/tests above; serial flags only on live-logging targets)
514	   to `write_oracle_config` as `broad_test_command`; Studio stamps it as `studio.broadTestCommand`
515	   and runs it verbatim at promote. Cost check: a serial live-logging suite is ~10–15 s/test, so
516	   the guarded subset (~60) ≈ 12–15 min vs ~180 tests ≈ 40 min for the whole suite — narrow to the
517	   guarded set (the ~120 unguarded tests contribute nothing), and parallelize the buffered targets
518	   on top of that.
519	
520	**Static completeness check BEFORE the run — advisory, ONE pass, never a loop.** Once the
521	instrumentation is in place but BEFORE you run the oracle, call
522	`check_action_coverage(pipeline_key, spec, src)` (`src` = the app source directory) **once**. Studio
523	extracts both sides **statically** (no test run) and returns two diffs — **NOT INSTRUMENTED** (a spec
524	action with no code event) and **NOT MODELED** (a code event with no spec action) — plus a `warning`
525	flag. Do not hand-run the grep pipeline. Tell the check how the code is actually annotated: if the
526	codebase logs through its own wrapper (`emit(node, "name", …)`), pass `log_fns: ["emit"]` so those
527	sites are detected reliably; if the config resolves actions via `actionTakenPath` (an imported spec
528	with a `lastAction`-style variant), pass `action_taken_path` — Studio then skips the name diffs
529	(they'd compare the wrong namespaces) and just lists the logged events.
530	
531	Studio rejects logged argument names that do not match the routed Quint action parameters; copy
532	identifiers from the action signature, while omitted arguments remain wildcard picks.
533	
534	This is a HINT, not a gate. The static grep matches a fixed set of instrumentation styles, so it
535	**cannot see** annotations it doesn't recognize: `actionTakenPath`/variant-tag logging (the name is a
536	runtime sum-type variant, never a literal at the call site), names routed through `actionNameMap`, or a
537	custom logging wrapper. When it misses those, it reports correctly-annotated actions as NOT
538	INSTRUMENTED. **The oracle run — not this grep — is ground truth** (the live `loggedTrace` proves what
539	actually fired). So:
540	- **Reconcile each NOT INSTRUMENTED entry against what YOU just wrote.** You authored the
541	  instrumentation; if you know you annotated that action (variant mode, a mapped name, or a wrapper the
542	  grep can't match), the detector simply missed your style — note it and move on. **Do NOT re-add it,
543	  and do NOT re-run the static check hoping for a different answer.**
544	- **If `warning` is set** (detection fell back to matching bare quoted names), treat the whole result
545	  as low-confidence — a single reconciliation pass, then run.
546	- **Only add a missing `log_action` when you genuinely forgot one** — a real, frequently-exercised
547	  action with no site anywhere. Do it once, here, before running. (**test-only model helper** not in
548	  `step()` → exclude; **failure-injection the tests can't trigger** → keep as a witness, instrument the
549	  real site, expect 0 hits, document.)
550	- **Never gate the run on a clean static result.** After at most one fix pass, PROCEED to the oracle
551	  run regardless of what NOT INSTRUMENTED still lists — the run resolves whether those are real gaps.
552	
553	Do NOT run the agent's how-well-annotated / blind-family triage here — that is a post-run analysis and
554	belongs after Phase 3 (below).
555	
556	**Run integration tests with a runner that gives per-test process isolation + a stable per-test slot.**
557	Multi-node integration suites typically assign each test a network port range from a per-test slot
558	index; without process-per-test isolation every test falls back to the same slot → identical ports →
559	mass `Address already in use` failures (and cascading `Connection refused`), which look like product
560	failures but are purely a runner mismatch. In **Rust** this means `cargo nextest run …` (nextest sets
561	`NEXTEST_TEST_GLOBAL_SLOT` → unique ports + process-per-test; plain `cargo test` leaves the slot unset
562	→ the port clash above). Process-per-test also makes the client's buffered flushes parallel-safe
563	(they are tagged with their test name), so nextest may keep its default parallelism — add
564	`--test-threads=1` only when the suite's transitions LIVE-log (a plain `log_action` firing on a
565	worker thread; per-node `log_action_for` buffering is process-global and therefore fine under
566	process-per-test). The PR's own scoped unit tests, which bind no ports, can stay on `cargo test`
567	(parallel is fine). Other runners: pick the equivalent isolated invocation.
568	
569	**Checklist before you finish the instrument step:**
570	- [ ] transition `logAction` sites are in shared/library code, not test wrappers
571	- [ ] the tests that drive this component across crates (incl. the integration suite) bind the
572	      `startTest` boundary via a shared helper
573	- [ ] the scoped PR run captured traces (`tests > 0`) so you know the annotation fires
574	- [ ] `studio.broadTestCommand` covers every test target (incl. any integration-test target) whose tests exercise the spec — parallel where buffered, serial only where live-logging

578	## Phase 3: Confirm wired — Studio runs the suite in the same call (your finish line)
579	
580	Once the config has a working `testCommand` and the instrumentation is in place, call
581	`confirm_wired(pipeline_key, oracle_config)`. Studio validates the config and IMMEDIATELY runs the
582	whole test suite through the oracle, returning the run's digest — do **not** follow it with a
583	`run_quint_oracle` call of your own. The call returns within about a minute — the result, or
584	FINISHER RUNNING with a `finisher_id`: the suite keeps running server-side, and
585	`await_finisher(finisher_id)` is the only wait (never re-call the tool, never watch processes).
586	The oracle maps each trace to valid sequences in the spec; mismatches are reported per test in
587	`report.json` and summarized in the digest.
588	
589	- **A clean run completes the pipeline in that same call** — the digest says PIPELINE DONE; STOP
590	  immediately, no finish calls, no summary.
591	- **`tests` empty / no traces captured**: the test boundaries are missing, the oracle didn't spawn
592	  the tests, or `QUINT_ORACLE_URL` wasn't set when the app loaded — fix that before anything else
593	  (set `QUINT_ORACLE_DEBUG=1` to see client traffic), then re-run with `run_quint_oracle`.
594	- **Unmatched failures**: the refine loop — use the digest and `report.json` to decide the
595	  next changes. **Classify each fix first.** A REPLAY-SIDE fix (the spec, `actionNameMap`,
596	  replay budgets, observations) never changes what the tests log, so Studio verifies it by
597	  replaying the STORED traces: `run_quint_oracle(pipeline_key)` returns in minutes, no tests
598	  execute, and a clean replay-only result completes the pipeline — it is the same verdict a
599	  fresh suite run would give, because the code is unchanged. A CAPTURE-SIDE fix (logging
600	  sites, test boundaries, logged arguments, `testCommand`) invalidates the stored traces —
601	  the next run captures for real; iterate those SCOPED with
602	  `run_quint_oracle(pipeline_key, test_command [...])` (the runner invocation for just the
603	  failing tests) and close with the full `run_quint_oracle(pipeline_key)`. Studio picks
604	  replay vs capture from the trace stamp automatically — never reason about staleness
605	  yourself. Fix independent failures together in one round, diagnosing the classes IN
606	  PARALLEL with read-only subagents (see "Error classes and triage"); go one at a time only
607	  when fixes could mask each other.
608	
609	Events explicitly scoped to other components are removed before replay and appear as the
610	non-fatal `foreign-action-excluded` warning. They are not evidence of a spec gap. An
611	`action-unresolved` failure after scope filtering targets the active component and remains a real
612	refinement blocker: fix its event name/mapping or the component's replay surface; never
613	blanket-ignore unknown actions.
614	
615	**A blind family is a SELF-CORRECT trigger, not a footnote (post-run analysis).** After the run, for
616	every spec family that is sim-reachable but has NO covering test, do NOT just report it — first rule
617	out that YOU caused it:
618	- **Did you under-scope?** A guarded test that covers it may have been filtered out (Phase 2b step 3).
619	  Broaden `broadTestCommand` to include every guarded module and re-check. (This is exactly how a
620	  value-sync filter can hide the `Invalid` family if the test that drives a bad certificate lives in
621	  another module.)
622	- **Is the branch annotated?** Confirm the library code for that outcome actually has a `log_action`
623	  (a conditional path that commits its transition off the main site; for a guarded operation's
624	  reject branch, the `outcome: "rejected"` tag — without it the matching guard scenario looks
625	  untested). If it's missing, that's YOUR bug — add it and re-run; the behavior was
626	  never observable, not untested. (The pre-run static check should have caught this, but a branch only
627	  reachable at runtime can still slip through.)
628	- **Only if scope is complete AND the branch is annotated AND still no test hits it** is it a GENUINE
629	  untested-behavior gap — surface it as a finding (the PR's error/edge path has no test). Never
630	  fabricate a test or weaken the spec to make it look covered.
631	
632	### Error classes and triage
633	
634	The oracle reports factual diagnostics through `failureKind`, `failureCode`, `failure`, and
635	`diagnostics`. Treat them as evidence for your own triage, not as a prescribed cause. Before
636	editing, decide whether the smallest next step is test-command scope, test boundary or
637	instrumentation, logged action mapping/arguments, model scope/granularity, or real product/model
638	divergence.
639

639	
640	**Diagnose independent failure classes IN PARALLEL.** When the digest names failures in more
641	than one independent class (different tests, different actions, different `failureCode`s), don't
642	walk them one after another: fan out one read-only `quint-code-researcher` subagent per class
643	(Agent tool, all in a single message). Give each ONE class and its exact evidence pointers — the
644	report path, the failing tests' names, their `loggedTrace` entries, the spec path, and the
645	relevant code paths — and ask for a grounded diagnosis at the right altitude (wiring / test
646	entrypoint / model scope, see below) plus the smallest proposed fix, each claim pinned to
647	`file:line` or a trace step. The subagents only diagnose; YOU read the returned diagnoses,
648	resolve conflicts (two classes may share one root cause — apply that fix once), make the edits,
649	and re-run scoped. Failures that plausibly share a cause go to the SAME subagent, never split.
650	
651	**Where the evidence lives.** The digest ends with the report's real path (`Full report: …`), and
652	`get_pipeline_state` carries it as `reportPath` — Studio redirects the config's `reportDir` to its
653	own app-data location, so never go hunting the filesystem for `report.json`. Each unmatched test's
654	report entry carries `diagnostics` and `loggedTrace` — the events retained for this component after
655	scope filtering, in order, with scopes and argument values. That trace is the ground truth: before choosing a fix, walk it against
656	the spec (which actions fired, in what order, what state they imply) instead of reasoning from the
657	failure text alone. Never re-capture traces yourself (no ad-hoc servers, no manual oracle runs).
658	
659	**Form a hypothesis at the right altitude before editing.** A replay failure can sit at three
660	levels, and the failure code alone does not tell you which:
661	- **Model scope/granularity** — the spec ties together what the code treats independently, misses
662	  an action the trace shows, or models at the wrong grain. Signature: the loggedTrace is sensible
663	  but no spec path can follow it.
664	- **Test entrypoint** — the configured tests drive the system through a different layer than the
665	  one you instrumented (or the wrong suite entirely). Signature: traces start mid-story or miss
666	  actions you know the code performs.
667	- **A small wiring tweak** — one name, one domain, one missing logged argument. Signature: the
668	  evidence names it exactly.
669	Verify the hypothesis in the evidence (loggedTrace, the spec, the test source) before editing;
670	a fix you can't ground in something you actually read is a guess.
671	
672	**Zoom out instead of digging in.** If the same `failureCode` survives two consecutive targeted
673	fixes, the problem is almost certainly NOT at the level you are fixing — stop tweaking, move one
674	level up (wiring → test entrypoint → model scope), and re-derive the hypothesis from the
675	loggedTrace. Repeating variations of the same fix is the rabbit hole this rule exists to prevent.
676	
677	Keep this stage's ownership narrow while applying the troubleshooting result:
678	- fix instrumentation, test boundaries, `testCommand`, logged event names, `actionNameMap`, and
679	  replay argument logging here;
680	- fix the spec only when the diagnostic shows the model or replay surface is genuinely wrong;
681	- stop once the oracle is runnable and captures traces; remaining spec gaps belong to the refine
682	  loop.
683	
684	**Iteration rule:** make one targeted change per run. Judge progress by whether the specific
685	failure you addressed changed, not by the unmatched total — under fail-fast (and whenever the
686	test scope shifts) counts are not comparable across runs. Stop when the run captures traces
687	(`tests > 0`) and has zero unmatched failures that are instrumentation issues — remaining spec
688	gaps are what the refine stage's loop resolves.
689

692	## Fixing the spec (a deliberate change, never a workaround)
693	
694	You authored the spec at the generate stage, so when a problem is genuinely spec work — a missing
695	action, a structural guard that misreads the code, a missing or unreachable observation, a domain
696	set that is too narrow, an argument the spec doesn't accept, or a nondet shape that cannot be
697	replayed from logged args — fix the spec directly. Treat it as spec work, not wiring:
698	
699	1. Make the smallest faithful change (add the action / relax the guard / add the observation / fix
700	   the replayable nondet/action surface), keeping the modelling discipline of `quint-modeling`.
701	   A new observation `val` is named after the behavior itself — no `obs_`/`track_` marker prefix
702	   (the config's `observations` list is what identifies it).
703	
704	**Refinement preserves the unhappy paths.** The suite you are refining against is mostly
705	happy-path; the spec is deliberately more adversarial than the tests — that asymmetry is the point,
706	not a mismatch to repair. **Never delete or weaken an adversarial action** (`crash`, `byzantineSend`,
707	a timeout race), a **correctness property**, or an **observation** to make a trace replay — those never
708	appear in logged traces (they are sim-side machinery), so they are never the cause of a replay
709	failure, and removing them only removes the spec's ability to catch bugs. Refine the *happy-path
710	fidelity* of the actions the logged trace actually exercises; if an adversarial action genuinely
711	interferes with replay, constrain it (a separate `any{}` arm, a budget `const`), don't excise it.
712	Dropping a correctness property or adversarial action is a **user decision** — surface it, with the consequence it
713	guards, and stop.
714	
715	**A guard conjunct that encodes a documented precondition is never "stricter than the real code" —
716	it IS the contract.** Relax a guard only when it misreads the code: a structural constraint you
717	inferred wrong, with no documented precondition behind it. When a trace fails replay on a conjunct
718	that encodes a documented contract, the unmatched trace is a candidate **violation finding** — the
719	code performed a transition its contract forbids, the highest-value find this pipeline can make.
720	Do not loosen the conjunct or widen its domain to make the trace replay; surface it and route it to
721	the reproduce lane, which pins the divergence as a failing contract-assertion test through the
722	app's own error API — red on the buggy code, green when the check lands.
723	2. Validate with `run_quint_check` until clean, and confirm every observation is still reachable
724	   — pass the config's **complete** observations list as `witnesses`, never a subset (a check
725	   that silently drops the observations that were failing proves nothing).
726	3. Re-run the oracle and confirm the failure class disappeared.
727	
728	**Never weaken the spec to match broken code — the spec is the ground truth.** A trace that
729	violates a safety invariant may be a real product bug: surface it to the user instead of editing
730	the spec around it. If the right model is genuinely unclear, stop and discuss with the user — that
731	is the highest-leverage review point.
732

735	## Investigate stage — triage the untested scenarios, observations, and blind families
736	
737	When a clean run leaves coverage gaps, the pipeline parks at **investigate**. The digest hands you
738	the findings; your job is a **verdict per finding**, recorded through
739	`submit_coverage_investigation`. A finding's subject is one of three kinds:
740	
741	| subject | shape | meaning |
742	|---|---|---|
743	| untested observation | the observation `val` name | an observation no test fired |
744	| blind family | the family's observation sequence | a sim-reachable behavior family no test lands in (untested *sequences*, not just untested flags) |
745	| guard scenario | `{"kind": "guard-scenario", "ruleId": "...", "guardId": ...}` — one transition rule paired with one guard conjunct | a falsifiable conjunct no test falsified: no test attempted the transition the conjunct forbids (no rejected-tagged attempt, no violation) |
746	
747	First rule out that the gap is self-inflicted, cheapest check first: spec reachability/polarity, an
748	unannotated branch, a missing `outcome: "rejected"` tag on the code's reject path (a tested reject
749	looks untested without it), `testCommand` scope. Fix and re-run `run_quint_oracle` — **a fixable
750	gap is never recorded around.**
751	
752	For each genuine gap, answer TWO questions, in order:
753	
754	1. **Would exercising it break the app?** Walk the sequence against the code: if a test drove
755	   exactly these transitions today, would the code crash, corrupt state, or violate the spec's
756	   invariants? You are reading code, not guessing — find the handler for each step and check what it
757	   assumes about the steps before it.
758	2. **Is the sequence itself wrong?** Even if nothing crashes: is this an ordering the user would
759	   call a bug on sight (a refund before a capture, a vote after a decision)? The spec permits it —
760	   should it?
761	
762	The answers classify the finding:
763	
764	| verdict | meaning | suggestedAction |
765	|---|---|---|
766	| `data-loss-or-corruption` | exercising it leaves the system in a state that is wrong and KEPT — data lost or overwritten, an invariant violated, an invalid record persisted (a crash on the way there counts). A latent bug the tests never poke | `reproduce` when the spec encodes a **contract the code should honor** (a guard conjunct stating a precondition) and you suspect the code doesn't — a contract-assertion test will PROVE the divergence; else `fix-first`, or `generate-test` to drive the fix |
767	| `unwanted-sequence` | runs fine, but the ordering itself is wrong — likely a missing guard in code AND a too-permissive spec worth flagging | `fix-first`, or `reproduce` if a guard conjunct pins a concrete assertion |
768	| `benign` | legal, harmless, just unexercised — worth a test only for coverage | `generate-test` or `none` |
769	| `out-of-scope` | reachable only through machinery outside this component's tests (e.g. requires fault injection) | `none` |
770	
771	Every finding is written **twice, in two registers** — different texts, not long and truncated
772	versions of one text. `reasoning` is the LONG one, for the next agent: what you actually **read**,
773	the code path and the assumption that does (or doesn't) hold, with paths, symbols and line numbers
774	— never "seems unlikely". It is never shown to the user. `summary` is the SHORT one and the ONLY
775	text Studio shows for the finding: two lines of plain prose, at most 220 characters, no paths, no
776	symbols, no line numbers — the way you would explain it out loud to whoever owns this code. Write
777	it fresh; the opening sentences of `reasoning` are not a summary, and Studio refuses the
778	submission without it. Recording completes the pipeline; `generate-test` verdicts
779	become the pre-selected families the next test-generation batch offers the user. **`reproduce`** is
780	the sharpest verdict: use it when the finding pins a contract the code may not honor (a guard
781	conjunct encoding a documented "must" the code may skip) — accepting it generates a
782	contract-assertion test that asserts the contract through the app's own error API, and its FAILURE
783	reproduces a real bug (a code-vs-model divergence), surfaced in the Bugs tab. Prefer it over
784	`generate-test` whenever the gap is a suspected unenforced contract, not just missing coverage.
785	**For a guard-scenario finding**, read the code for the conjunct's check: if you cannot find it,
786	the contract may be unenforced — the verdict is `data-loss-or-corruption` with suggestedAction `reproduce`,
787	and the contract test feeding the forbidden input and asserting the rejection is exactly what
788	proves it. **A VIOLATED scenario** — a real test already performed the transition the conjunct
789	forbids — is not a triage question but a confirmed code-vs-contract divergence: `reproduce` it to
790	pin the divergence as a failing contract-assertion test (red on the buggy code, green when the
791	check lands); never resolve it by loosening the guard.
792	
793	---
794	
795	## Instrumentation by Language / Framework
796	
797	### Go (net/http or chi)
798	
799	```go
800	func OracleMiddleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
801	    return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
802	        rw := &responseCapture{ResponseWriter: w}
803	        next.ServeHTTP(rw, r)
804	        if rw.status == 200 {
805	            if trace, ok := r.Context().Value(oracleTraceKey{}).(OracleTrace); ok {
806	                oracle.LogAction(trace.Action, trace.Args) // fire-and-forget
807	            }
808	        }
809	    })
810	}
811	```
812	
813	### Python (FastAPI / Flask)
814	
815	```python
816	import os, httpx
817	ORACLE_URL = os.getenv("QUINT_ORACLE_URL")
818	
819	async def log_action(action: str, args: list[dict]):
820	    if not ORACLE_URL: return
821	    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
822	        await client.put(f"{ORACLE_URL}/log", json={
823	            "action": action,
824	            "arguments": args,
825	            "scopes": ["cart"],  # exact eventScope from the config
826	        })
827	```
828	
829	### Rust (Axum)
830	
831	Use tower middleware: attach an `OracleTrace` extension before `next.run(req)`, read it after the
832	response is built, log only on 2xx.
833	
834	---
835	
836	## Common Pitfalls
837	
838	| Pitfall | Fix |
839	|---|---|
840	| Shelling out to `ls`/`cat`/`find`/`grep` | Use `Read`/`Glob`/`Grep` |
841	| Running quint yourself (any subcommand) | The first oracle run rides `confirm_wired`; re-runs go through `run_quint_oracle`; spec validation goes through `run_quint_check` |
842	| Contorting the spec to make a run pass | Spec fixes are deliberate changes (see *Fixing the spec*) — validated with `run_quint_check`, never a guard-loosening workaround |
843	| Deleting an adversarial action / correctness property to fix a replay failure | Sim-side machinery never appears in logged traces — fix the happy-path action the trace exercises; removal is a user decision to surface |
844	| Writing a new test to raise coverage | Never — only instrument existing tests; coverage gaps are for the user to fill later |
845	| Producing a coverage report / running the full pass | Not your job — finish once the oracle is runnable; Studio runs the coverage pass next |
846	| Putting `logAction` in test code | It goes in the application code; the only test-side change is the shared `startTest` hook |
847	| Logging before the outcome is known | `logAction` once the operation resolves — a completed transition logs plain; a rejection of a guarded operation logs the same action tagged `outcome: "rejected"` (log from the branch that ran, never speculatively before) |
848	| Loosening a guard to make a trace replay | A conjunct encoding a documented precondition IS the contract — the failing trace is a candidate violation finding; surface it and route to the reproduce lane, never widen the guard or its domain |
849	| Action name mismatch | Add/fix `actionNameMap`; unmapped logged events must equal Quint action names |
850	| Arg/domain name mismatch | Copy exact identifiers from the spec — don't retype |
851	| Missing `startTest` | Each test needs a boundary, or traces merge / report `trace-empty` |
852	| Unscoped event rejected | Construct the logger with the config's exact `eventScope`; the public clients expose no global transition API |
853	| `event-unscoped` failure | Instrumentation emitted an ownerless transition. Repair the named application logging sites with the correct component-scoped logger and rerun; never edit the spec for this code |
854	| `tests` empty in report | Tests not spawned by the oracle, or `QUINT_ORACLE_URL` unset at app load, or no `startTest` |
855	| Running oracle server manually, then tests separately | Oracle gets zero traces — let `quint oracle` spawn the tests |
856	| Replay budget failures | Add missing logged picks when possible; raise `unguidedStepBudget` or `stepReplayBudget` only deliberately |
857	| Oracle crashes with `fetch failed` mid-run | Studio's runs pin `--max-samples 100`; add `maxSteps: 20` in the config if a run still struggles |
858	| `POST /create` inlines sub-resources | Some transitions never hit their endpoint — fetch the created resource and emit the missing `logAction` conditionally when `QUINT_ORACLE_URL` is set |
859	| Old `tracks`/`trackGroups` config keys | Use `observations`/`observationGroups` |
860	| Hunting the filesystem for `report.json` | The digest's `Full report:` line and `get_pipeline_state`'s `reportPath` carry the real path (Studio redirects the config's `reportDir`) |
861	| `foreign-action-excluded` warning | Expected cross-component traffic was scoped out before replay. Verify the scope only if the ownership looks wrong; do not add the foreign action to this component's map/spec |
862	| Active `action-unresolved` failure | The event explicitly targets this component but resolves to no replay action. Fix the scoped call/action name or `actionNameMap`; do not ignore unknown actions globally |
863	| Comparing unmatched counts across runs | Not comparable under fail-fast or when test scope changed — judge by whether the specific failure you addressed changed |
864	| Compile-checking outside the project's build environment | Use the same wrapper the config's `testCommand`/`buildCommand` already uses (e.g. `nix develop --command`, a repo script) instead of rediscovering the toolchain |
865	| Promote's broad coverage finds nothing | Candidate targets' tests lack a `startTest` boundary, the transition is logged in test wrappers (not library code), or `studio.broadTestCommand` omits the integration-test target — see Phase 2b |
866	| Async/actor test's trace is empty or mis-attributed | Its transition LIVE-logs from a worker thread (e.g. a `tokio` worker) — a plain `log_action` there is untagged and lands in the daemon's serial slot; `start_test` POSTs up front so it attributes, but only if that suite runs **serially** (one test at a time). Add the serial flag to THAT target; buffered targets keep their parallelism |
867	| Integration tests mass-fail with `Address already in use` / `Connection refused` | The suite assigns ports from a per-test slot index and you ran it without process-per-test isolation (every test used the same slot → same ports). Run it isolated instead (in Rust, **`cargo nextest run`** — parallel is fine when logging is buffered) — not a product bug |
868	
869	---
870	
871	## End-of-Skill Output
872	
873	When the wiring is complete (config wired + instrumentation in place), deliver:
874	
875	1. **Oracle config** at `quint-oracle.<key>.json` — the draft with your added `testCommand`
876	   (and `buildCommand` if needed); confirmed observations left untouched.
877	2. **Oracle client** vendored at `quint-specs/oracle-client/<language>/` (via `vendor_oracle_client`)
878	   with the dependency wired in — or the existing client's mapping extended if one was already set up.
879	3. **Instrumentation diff** — component-scoped `logAction` calls in the application code + the `startTest` boundary
880	   wired into the existing tests (via a shared hook); no new tests, no logic in test wrappers.
881	4. **Any spec fixes you made along the way** (what changed and why), and any suspected product
882	   bugs surfaced rather than modeled around.
883	
884	Then `confirm_wired` — the run it chains produces the coverage. Do **not** produce a coverage
885	report or recommend tests yourself.
886	
887	## Handoff signal (REQUIRED)
888	
889	Quint Studio registers that you are done by **a concrete artifact on disk**, never by you narrating
890	that you finished — so always finish by producing the artifact, then the finisher call:
891	
892	- **Wiring (oracle setup):** the Studio oracle config `quint-oracle.<key>.json` must contain a
893	  working `testCommand` (and `buildCommand` if the suite needs a rebuild). Wire it **in place**;
894	  do not leave the command only in a separate mapping/allowlist config. Then call `confirm_wired`
895	  — Studio validates that file and chains the first oracle run onto it, returning the digest.
896	- **Component Refine stage:** address every entry in `refinement.requests`, validate changed
897	  models with `run_quint_check`, call `submit_refinement`, then call `run_quint_oracle`.
898	- **Post-test refinement (`refine:<component>`):** address every request from the kickoff and
899	  validate changed models, then call `run_quint_oracle` directly. Starting the run checkpoints
900	  the validation; there is no separate submit call. A clean run settles the refinement and the

900	  the validation; there is no separate submit call. A clean run settles the refinement and the
901	  controller resumes pending test generation after releasing the shared Oracle slot.

1	# Oracle client implementations — read on demand
2	
3	Load this ONLY when you actually need to add or port a client (the skill's Phase 1
4	says when). The client API contract lives in the skill.
5	
6	## Rust, TypeScript and Go — vendored by Studio, never hand-written
7	
8	Call the **`vendor_oracle_client` MCP tool** with the language. Studio writes the
9	library into `quint-specs/oracle-client/<language>/` and the response carries the
10	exact dependency line, import, and call-site snippets:
11	
12	- **Rust** — a local crate; consumed with
13	  `quint-oracle-client = { path = "<rel path to>/quint-specs/oracle-client/rust" }`
14	  (zero-dependency, no-op unless `QUINT_ORACLE_URL` is set; if the repo is a cargo
15	  workspace, add the vendored dir to `workspace.exclude` or `members`).
16	- **TypeScript** — a local no-build npm package; consumed with a
17	  `"quint-oracle-client": "file:quint-specs/oracle-client/typescript"` devDependency
18	  and `import { startTest, scope } from 'quint-oracle-client'`.
19	- **Go** — a local stdlib-only module; consumed with
20	  `require quint-oracle-client v0.0.0` plus
21	  `replace quint-oracle-client => ./quint-specs/oracle-client/go` in the consuming
22	  go.mod, and `import quintoracle "quint-oracle-client"`.
23	
24	Never edit files under `quint-specs/oracle-client/` (Studio-managed; overwritten on
25	re-vendor) and never re-paste an HTTP client when the tool covers the stack. The
26	vendored directory is meant to be **committed** — that is what makes the
27	instrumentation build and report on other machines.
28	
29	```rust
30	// HOLD the guard for the whole test scope. start_test registers the test with the
31	// daemon IMMEDIATELY (so a transition firing on a tokio worker thread — async/actor
32	// tests — still attributes to this test) AND buffers any same-thread steps, flushing
33	// them atomically on drop. Two delivery paths, one rule:
34	//   * synchronous tests (transition on the test thread): buffered + drop-flushed, so
35	//     bounded-PARALLEL sync tests never corrupt each other (--test-threads=N is fine);
36	//   * async/actor tests (transition on a worker thread): live-attributed to the slot
37	//     start_test set — so those tests MUST run SERIALLY (--test-threads=1).
38	// A bare statement flushes early and loses the buffering — always bind the guard.
39	let _t = quint_oracle_client::start_test("<test name>");
40	let oracle = quint_oracle_client::scope(&["<eventScope from config>"]);
41	oracle.log_action("ACTION", &[
42	    quint_oracle_client::Arg { name: "user", value: user.into(), domain: Some("USERS") },
43	]);
44	```
45	
46	```typescript
47	// The TS client buffers each test's steps and flushes them atomically at end() —
48	// wire the boundary through ONE shared hook, not per test:
49	import { startTest, scope, TestGuard } from 'quint-oracle-client';
50	const oracle = scope('<eventScope from config>');
51	let t: TestGuard;
52	beforeEach(function () { t = startTest(this.currentTest?.fullTitle() ?? expect.getState().currentTestName!); });
53	afterEach(async () => { await t.end(); });
54	// Instrumented application sites:
55	await oracle.logAction('ACTION', [{ name: 'user', value: user, domain: 'USERS' }]);
56	// Parallel jest/vitest workers are fine (flushes are test-tagged); avoid
57	// test.concurrent within one file, and add --runInBand only when logging is live.
58	```
59	
60	```go
61	// The Go client keeps ONE process-global current test (Go has no goroutine-local
62	// storage): StartTest registers the test with the daemon immediately AND buffers
63	// steps from ANY goroutine, flushing them atomically at End(). Within a package Go
64	// already runs tests serially — avoid t.Parallel() in instrumented suites.
65	// `go test ./...` package-parallelism is fine: flushes are test-tagged, so the
66	// daemon attributes interleaved processes correctly.
67	import quintoracle "quint-oracle-client"
68	
69	var oracle = quintoracle.Scope("<eventScope from config>")
70	
71	func TestSomething(t *testing.T) {
72		g := quintoracle.StartTest(t.Name())
73		t.Cleanup(g.End) // flushes the trace atomically
74		// … exercise the code …
75	}
76	
77	// Instrumented application sites:
78	oracle.LogAction("ACTION", quintoracle.Arg{Name: "user", Value: user, Domain: "USERS"})
79	```
80	
81	## Implementing your own client (any language, or a target that can't take the dep)
82	
83	Adapt the vendored implementations when you need a client in another stack — the
84	**`quint-oracle-client` Rust crate source** (`quint-specs/oracle-client/rust/src/lib.rs`
85	once vendored) is the canonical reference; the vendored `index.js` is the same design in
86	JS. A custom client in any language MUST replicate these semantics:
87	
88	- **No-op unless `QUINT_ORACLE_URL` is set** — so adding the calls never affects normal builds/tests.
89	- **Protocol:** `POST {url}/test/<percent-encoded name>` to begin a test; `PUT {url}/log` with body
90	  `{ "action": "<name>", "test?": "<test-name>", "arguments": [ { "name", "value", "domain?" } ], "scopes": ["<component-key>"] }`
91	  per transition. A transition genuinely owned by several component abstractions may list several
92	  keys. Instrumentation must not omit `scopes`; the oracle rejects unscoped events. Plain
93	  HTTP/1.1, `Connection: close`; drain the response so the daemon finishes before the socket closes.
94	- **Attribution (the subtle part — the daemon keeps ONE fallback `current_test` slot, but tagged
95	  steps bypass it):**
96	  - **Register the test up front** — send `POST /test/<name>` at `start_test`, BEFORE any step, so a
97	    transition that fires outside the buffered context still lands in this test's slot.
98	  - **Buffer the test's steps** and flush them at test end (guard drop / `end()`) with every `/log`
99	    body TAGGED — `"test": "<name>"` — so the daemon routes each step to its trace even when
100	    another worker PROCESS's flush interleaves. Keep the process-global flush lock (it orders
101	    threads within the process).
102	  - **Send `POST /test-end/<percent-encoded name>` after the flush** — it triggers the daemon's
103	    eager fail-fast check for that test immediately (the suite's last test has no next `/test`
104	    boundary, so without the end signal it is never eagerly checked).
105	  - **Un-buffered transitions** (a context the buffer can't see) send live UNTAGGED `PUT /log` into
106	    the fallback slot; suites relying on that path MUST run serially (one test at a time).
107	  - With tagging in place, parallel test WORKERS (jest workers, nextest processes, separate
108	    integration binaries) are safe for buffered logging; only live-logging suites need serial.

# The image installs from uv.lock, so these are the only pins in the repo — the Dockerfile
# no longer carries a second copy that can drift out of step with this file.
[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=9.1.1",
    "httpx2>=2.10.0",
    "ruff>=0.16.1",
    "ty>=0.0.71",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
# target-version is inferred from requires-python — one place to change it.

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "C4"]
ignore = ["E501"]  # Line length is the formatter's job.

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# app.py imports store and didkey as plain top-level modules — they ship flat into the
# image and are imported by path, never installed. Telling ruff they are first-party
# keeps the import blocks sorted the way the code is actually laid out.
known-first-party = ["app", "didkey", "store"]

[tool.ty.environment]
# Same reason: `import store` resolves only with src/ on the path. mcp/src is the
# separately-published MCP wrapper — its own package, checked here so it cannot rot.
extra-paths = ["./src", "./mcp/src"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]

# Not an installable package: src/ is copied into the image and imported by path.
# Without this, uv tries to build a wheel and fails.
[tool.uv]
package = false

# Autonomous loop check

You're being invoked on a timer while the user is away or occupied. The point is to keep work moving forward without the user driving every step — finishing things they started, maintaining PRs they're building, catching problems before they come back to find them. You're a steward, not an initiator. The user set you loose on their work, and the value you provide comes from reliably advancing things they've already set in motion, not from finding new things to do.

The key tension to navigate: the user trusts you enough to run autonomously, but that trust is easily lost. Acting on what the conversation already established is safe and valuable. Inventing new work or making irreversible changes without clear authorization erodes trust fast. When you're unsure whether something falls into "continuing established work" or "inventing new work," lean toward the former only when the transcript provides clear evidence the user wanted it done. If you find yourself reaching for justifications about why a push is probably fine, that's a signal to wait.

## What to act on

The current conversation is your highest-signal source — re-read the transcript above, since everything there is something the user was actively engaged with. The strongest signal is an in-progress PR you've been building together: review comments to address and resolve, failing CI checks to diagnose (and re-enqueue if they're flakes), merge conflicts to fix. The goal is to get the PR into a state where it's ready to merge pending only human review — the user shouldn't come back to find a PR blocked on things you could have handled. After that, look for unfinished implementation where the last exchange left something half-done, and explicit "I'll also..." or "next I'll..." commitments the conversation made and didn't honor. Weaker but still real: dangling questions you could now answer, verification steps that were skipped, edge cases that were mentioned but not handled, and natural continuations that don't require new decisions.

If you find anything in this category, act on it — actually do the work, don't describe what could be done. Run the tests, don't say "you could run the tests." The whole point of autonomous operation is that work gets done while the user is away.

When the conversation transcript has nothing left, the current branch's pull/merge request on the user's SCM is the next-best place to look. This is maintenance work — valuable, but lower priority than continuing the user's active work. Find the PR/MR for the current branch via the SCM's CLI, then check three things: CI status, unresolved review threads, and whether the branch has fallen behind the base. For failing CI, pull the failing job's logs and diagnose before acting — flaky-shaped failures (timeout, runner died, transient network) can be re-enqueued; real failures need a reproduction and a minimal fix. For unresolved review threads, fetch the comment, address the feedback, push, and resolve the thread via, for example, the GitHub GraphQL `resolveReviewThread` mutation (or the equivalent for whichever SCM the project uses). Before pushing anything, check whether someone else has pushed to the branch while you were working — if so, rebase (don't merge) to keep history clean.

When CI is green, threads are clear, and there's idle time, sweeping the branch for issues is a good use of that time — bug-hunt or simplification passes catch problems before reviewers do, saving everyone a round-trip.

If everything is genuinely quiet — no conversation work, no PR maintenance — say so in one sentence and stop. No summary of what you checked, no list of what you might do later. The user will see your message in the transcript when they come back; three consecutive "nothing to do" results means you should scale back to a quick CI check and stop, not narrate.

```python
"""Best-effort HTTP client for the Quint oracle daemon.
...

from __future__ import annotations

import http.client
import json
import os
import urllib.parse

_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 2

def _base_url() -> str | None:
    return os.environ.get("QUINT_ORACLE_URL") or None

def _request(method: str, path: str, body: dict | None = None) -> None:
    base = _base_url()
    if not base:
        return
    parsed = urllib.parse.urlsplit(base)
    try:
        conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(
            parsed.hostname, parsed.port or 80, timeout=_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
        )
        try:
            headers = {"Connection": "close"}
            payload = b""
            if body is not None:
                headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
                payload = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
            conn.request(method, path, body=payload, headers=headers)
            conn.getresponse().read()
        finally:
            conn.close()
    except OSError:
        pass

def start_test(name: str) -> None:
    _request("POST", f"/test/{urllib.parse.quote(name, safe='')}")

def end_test(name: str) -> None:
    _request("POST", f"/test-end/{urllib.parse.quote(name, safe='')}")

class Scope:
    def __init__(self, *component_keys: str) -> None:
        self._scopes = list(component_keys)

    def log_action(self, action: str, arguments: list[dict]) -> None:
        _request("PUT", "/log", {"action": action, "arguments": arguments, "scopes": self._scopes})

def scope(*component_keys: str) -> Scope:
    return Scope(*component_keys)
```
